transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Roberto Diaz (Acme - Head of Search), Maya Chen (Acme - ML Eng), Nina Park (Acme - Prod)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Jordan, i'm the AE for your account. Priya is our solutions engineer who'll do the deep dive. Roberto, Maya — thanks for your time.
[00:12] Roberto (Acme): yep thanks, we appreciate it. short on time so would like to see embeddings + rerank flow, mostly around improving search relevance for product search.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): cool, we'll do a quick walkthrough of the Hosted API endpoints for embeddings and the rerank endpoint, then show the Console, and end with recommendations from Optimize for latency/cost. feel free to interrupt.
[00:30] Priya: a quick qual — what's your current stack for search? are you using Elastic or a vector store?
[00:36] Roberto: we run Elastic as primary, added Pinecone for a couple POCs. indexing pipeline is in airflow, we store product metadata in postgres. search is hybrid today but relevance is kinda inconsistent on long tail queries.
[00:47] Maya: our main constraints are latency under 150ms p95 for core searches, cost budget is tight and we can't add lots of infra engineering. also security — SOC2 and SSO are must-haves.
[01:00] Jordan: understood. Redwood hosted can do embedding generation at request time or pre-compute and store vectors; rerank can be applied at query time to a small recall set to keep latency down. we'll demo both patterns.
[01:14] [01:15] Priya: opening the demo — here's the Hosted API docs page. first, embeddings endpoint, you POST text and receive vector, we support multiple embedding models and dims. quick note: vector dims we usually suggest 768 or 1024 depending on model, you can choose.
[01:30] Priya: example curl — curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input": "red leather jacket, size M"}'
[01:40] Priya: and you'll get a JSON with embedding array, then push to your store (e.g., Pinecone, Faiss, Elastic vector fields). transcription note: sometimes the auto transcripts say 'KV cash' — that's our KV cache mention later.
[01:55] Maya: quick q — do you provide integrated vector DB hosting or do we bring our own?
[02:00] Priya: Hosted API doesn't host vector DBs long-term but we have quick integrations, and Redwood Optimize will give batching and caching suggestions. many customers use Pinecone or Elastic's vector fields and we have example connectors.
[02:12] Jordan: re: security, we are SOC2, support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and you can use customer-managed keys with Private deployments; for Hosted we offer encryption at rest and strict audit logging.
[02:28] Roberto: good. show rerank — how does that fit?
[02:33] Priya: rerank endpoint takes a query and a small set of candidate documents (like top 100) and returns a re-ordered list with scores. key for latency is keep the candidate set small (<=100) and use streaming to cut time. rerank runs a cross-encoder model which is higher cost but much better for precision on relevance.
[02:55] Priya: demoing the re-rank request now. sample payload: query + candidates array with ids + text snippets. we'll show a before/after relevance.
[03:10] [03:15] Priya: showing sample results — before: top results include out-of-stock items and poor category matches, after rerank we push higher semantic matches. note: transcription may say 're-rank' as 'rerank' or 're rank' in different places.
[03:30] Maya: what's the expected latency impact? if rerank adds 100ms to the critical path it's tough.
[03:36] Priya: depends — if you do hybrid: produce top-k with Elastic NN search (10-30ms), then call rerank on top 50, the rerank call can add ~40-120ms depending on model and size. Redwood Optimize can recommend a smaller rerank model or quantized variant to trade a bit of quality for latency. also caching prefix embeddings reduces compute for repeated queries.
[03:58] Roberto: cost ballpark?
[04:02] Jordan: we usually show two patterns in TCO: (1) pre-compute embeddings + cheap vector search + infrequent rerank on small recall sets; (2) embed & rerank at query time for freshness. Pattern (1) is usually much cheaper. we'll send a TCO sheet.
[04:20] Priya: opening the Console — here's per-route token and latency breakdowns, you can see per-model cost, per-customer usage, traces. there's an example alert for regression on relevance tied to eval prompt sets.
[04:35] Priya: Console also surfaces Optimize suggestions: batching window adjustments, KV cache TTLs (we call it KV cache to store prefix states), and quantization profiles for rerank models to reduce memory. sometimes auto transcripts mis-spell quantization as 'quantisation' or 'quantize' inconsistently.
[04:55] Maya: can we run a canary with a specific subset of users?
[04:59] Jordan: yes, rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic fallback based on latency and quality metrics. you can pin traffic percentages to hosted vs dedicated pools.
[05:12] Priya: technical deep dive — model selection. for rerank we generally recommend a cross-encoder tuned for relevance (eg redwood-cross-1) and for embeddings a dense vector model (redwood-embed-1). we provide compatibility notes for dimension sizes and recommended normalization.
[05:33] Maya: are there prebuilt evaluation harnesses? we have a 10k query test set we use for offline eval.
[05:38] Priya: yes, we can run your eval set in our POC harness, produce precision/recall, MRR, and compute uplift. that will be part of the POC deliverables.
[05:48] Roberto: what about data residency — can hosted keep data in eu-west?
[05:52] Jordan: hosted has region controls; for stricter residency you can use Private with a VPC or on-prem. we'll flag that in security docs.
[05:59] [06:00] Priya: quick note on engineer friction — our SDKs are minimal: send embeddings, store vectors, call rerank. sample node/python code in the repo. i'll paste snippets to the follow-up.
[06:12] Maya: any gotchas with tokenization differences affecting embeddings?
[06:16] Priya: minor differences across models, but we normalize text and provide recommended preproc. also Optimize suggests when to truncate vs chunk long descriptions for best recall.
[06:28] Jordan: let's walk a simple end-to-end: user types query -> Elastic top100 -> call Redwood rerank on top 50 -> return top 10. we showed latency considerations and cost per rerank call.
[06:45] Priya: showing sample benchmark numbers from another customer as reference — precompute pattern had p95 120ms and cost X, hybrid with rerank had p95 180ms but doubled precision on long-tail queries. caveat: sample workloads vary.
[07:05] Maya: ok that's helpful. can you run a quick smoke test against a small dataset now?
[07:10] Priya: i can do a synthetic sample — i'll call embeddings endpoint for three product titles and then call rerank on 5 candidates.
[07:20] [07:30] Priya: (typing sounds) sending call... response returned, embeddings length 1024, tiny float noise in transcript shows as 'one zero two four' sometimes in auto text.
[07:42] Priya: rerank returning scores, see candidate 3 jumped to top because semantic similarity matched synonyms in description.
[07:50] Roberto: nice. this mirrors problems we see.
[07:55] Jordan: next steps — we'll provision a short-lived hosted API key and provide code snippets, share pricing and security pack, and run a POC with your 10k queries.
[08:07] Maya: timeframe for POC? we want results in 2 weeks ideally.
[08:12] Priya: we can run initial POC benchmark in 1-2 weeks depending on dataset readiness. we'll need sample queries and a few re-rank candidate sets.
[08:22] Jordan: ok wrapping up — recap action items and owners.
[08:28] Roberto: thanks all, good session.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR artifacts (misspellings of product names and code snippets), speaker turns sometimes consolidated. References to Console, Optimize, KV cache, rerank endpoint, redwood-embed-1, redwood-cross-1, region controls, SOC2, SAML, RBAC, and POC harness were made.
